kurz: Vegetables are plant cells full of water, held together by a glue. Cooking decides three things: bite, colour and flavour.
bild_im_kopf: Like a wall of water balloons: the mortar decides the bite, and the colour of the balloons changes with heat and acid.
was_passiert: Heat dissolves the glue between the cells, and the [[pektin-abbau|vegetables soften]]. Green vegetables turn olive green with long cooking; red ones react to acid and alkali. Dry, strong heat browns the surface and brings sweet roasted aromas.
warum_wichtig: If you know what acid, time and heat do to vegetables, you get [[knackig|crisp]] beans, bright broccoli and deeply browned onions.
faustregeln: Cook green vegetables briefly in plenty of water, then refresh in cold water. Plenty of water barely cools when they go in, so cooking stays short.
For roasting: dry, spaced out, hot.
Acid only at the end if vegetables are meant to soften.
